text:
kevin: Heads up — hit a reproducible hang in the Go generator/sampleapp when auth refresh blocks mid-stream. Iterator just stops yielding and goroutines pile up.

ana: Hmm, can you paste a tiny repro? Is this the pull-style Generator or the streaming callback pattern?

kevin: Pull-style Generator. Minimal usage looks like this and then it stalls when auth refetch blocks on network; cancelling the caller ctx doesn't wake Next():

```go
// simplified repro
it := client.Generator(ctx, req)
for {
  tok, err := it.Next()
  if err == io.EOF { break }
  if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
  process(tok)
}
```

kevin: The auth refresh runs in background and sometimes blocks (backoff/network). When that happens, Next() seems stuck inside an internal recv and ctx cancel doesn't interrupt it.

marta: Sounds like an ownership/cancellation mismatch. Next() not taking a ctx is the root cause here — users expect per-call cancellation. Two obvious options: add Next(ctx) or add an explicit Interrupt/Close that unblocks Next().

samir: Agreed. Current semantics rely on canceling the root ctx passed to Generator, but in practice we hand the iterator around and contexts get layered. API suggestion: Next(ctx) + Close(). For debug we could also add TryNext() which returns immediately if blocked.

ana: Workaround for now: spawn a goroutine that calls it.Close() when your parent context is Done(). Ugly but works. Example:

```go
go func() {
  <-ctx.Done()
  _ = it.Close()
}()
```

kevin: I'll open a GH issue with the repro + goroutine dump. Quick snippet of blocked goroutines when it hangs:

```
goroutine 42 [chan receive, 120 minutes]:
main.(*generator).Next(0xc0000...)
	/.../sdk/generator.go:123 +0x85
created by main.main
```

marta: Internal change could be to make the internal send/select use the user ctx: `select { case out <- item: case <-ctx.Done(): return }`. That prevents stuck sends, but we need a policy for dropped tokens/backpressure.

samir: Right — if we select on ctx.Done() we might silently drop tokens. Options: buffered channel + documented semantics, or make Next(ctx) return an explicit error if upstream ctx canceled so caller can decide to reconsume.

ana: Can we add a unit test in sampleapp that simulates long auth latency to catch regressions? :thumbsup:

kevin: Yes — I'll add a test that stubs Auth.Refresh to block and asserts Close()/cancel unblocks Next(). Will attach to GH issue.

marta: For compatibility I'd prefer adding `Next(ctx)` and keeping `Next()` as legacy wrapper that uses the generator root ctx (but mark deprecated). That lets callers opt-in to per-call cancellation.

kevin: SGTM. Also worth documenting auth refresh contract: "refresh must avoid blocking user-facing goroutines" — but we can't rely on it, so API change is still needed.

deploy-bot: deploy failed for go-sdk v0.26.4 on CI: test-gen-cancelation flaky — https://ci.redwood/1234

samir: Likely related — triaging.

ana: Created GH issue #3421 with repro, goroutine dump, and suggested Next(ctx) API: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/issues/3421

kevin: Thanks — I'll draft the PR with tests + sampleapp docs: "How to properly cancel generator iteration".

marta: Add to changelog and note potential ergonomic change; if we deprecate Next() we should call it out in the migration guide.

kevin: Sounds good. I'll ping eng-runtime for any concerns about internal channel/buffering before sending PR. Thanks all!
